title: Salvation does not require knowing every canonical book; reception may still be immediate
source_text: XIII. Jam autem ad salutem cujusque non est necessarium ut singulos Scripturae libros, et singulas eorum partes recipiat et agnoscat. Itaque non mirum est si omnes qui spiritum fidei et revelationis, aliquo saltem gradu, acceperunt, ignorent tamen quasdam Scripturae partes, et in eo fallantur quod aliquem librum, qui vere divinus est, humanum esse opinentur: Et vicissim librum aliquem, qui tantum est foetus ingenii humani, divinitus conscriptum existiment. Ac plane injustum est, et contra rationem a simplici quovis fideli exigere ut per se statim internoscere possit quamvis Canonici libri particulam a portiuncula libri Apocryphi. Nec enim ad ejus salutem hoc requiritur. Inde tamen non sequitur eos qui libros istos a quibusdam rejectos, aut ignotos amplectuntur, et fide suscipiunt, eos inquam istud non facere immediate per testimonium et illuminationem internam Spiritus sancti, quo majore hac in parte copia donati sunt, sed mediante Ecclesiae testimonio et authoritate, tanquam fidei suae fundamento.
pass_a_gloss: Now however it is not necessary for each one's salvation that he receive and acknowledge every book of Scripture, and every part of them. And so it is no wonder if all who have received the spirit of faith and revelation, at least in some degree, nevertheless are ignorant of certain parts of Scripture, and are mistaken in this, that they think some book which is truly divine to be human: And conversely think some book which is only a product of human wit to have been written by divine inspiration. And it is plainly unjust, and against reason, to require of any simple believer that he be able at once by himself to tell apart any particle of a Canonical book from a scrap of an Apocryphal book. For this is not required for his salvation. Yet it does not follow from that that those who embrace and take on faith those books rejected or unknown by some do not do that immediately by the inward testimony and illumination of the Holy Spirit, with which they have been gifted in greater supply in this part, but by the intervening of the Church's testimony and authority as the foundation of their faith.
pass_b_english: It is not necessary for anyone's salvation to receive and acknowledge every book of Scripture and every part of them.

So it is no wonder if all who have received the spirit of faith and revelation, even in some measure, still miss certain parts of Scripture — taking a truly divine book for human, or conversely taking a mere product of human wit for something written by divine inspiration.

It is plainly unjust, and against reason, to demand that any ordinary believer be able at once by himself to tell any scrap of a Canonical book from a scrap of an Apocryphal one. Salvation does not require that.

Yet it does not follow that those who embrace books some have rejected or not known, and take them on faith, do so only through the Church's testimony and authority as faith's foundation, and not immediately by the Spirit's inward testimony and illumination — with which they have been given a greater supply in this part.

lemmas.gloss: a scrap / small portion of an Apocryphal book
by the intervening of the Church's testimony

choices.why: Tiny fragment recognition test is unjust.
